title: Secure Remote Access: Session Manager, Client VPN & Verified Access
summary: Admin and user access to private resources without bastion hosts or open SSH ports.
tldr: **Session Manager**: shell access with no inbound ports, no SSH keys and no bastion. Needs the SSM Agent, an instance profile with `AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore`, and a path to SSM (NAT or VPC endpoints).
**EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint**: SSH/RDP to private instances with no public IP and no agent, controlled by IAM. Use it when the SSM Agent can't be installed.
**Client VPN**: managed OpenVPN for users who need network-level access to the VPC. **Verified Access**: zero-trust, per-application access without a VPN, checking user identity and device posture.

keyFacts.text: Interface endpoints Session Manager needs in a VPC with no internet path (older agents also used `ec2messages`).
IAM permission `ec2-instance-connect:OpenTunnel` controls who can use an Instance Connect Endpoint; the instance SG must allow SSH from the endpoint's SG.
Session Manager can log session activity to S3 or CloudWatch Logs and every session start is in CloudTrail.
Verified Access evaluates each request against a user trust provider (such as IAM Identity Center) and an optional device trust provider.

traps: Session Manager port forwarding still needs the SSM Agent; it won't help where agents are banned.
A hardened bastion with a restricted CIDR is still a bastion; the question usually wants Session Manager or Instance Connect Endpoint.
Client VPN grants network access, not per-application authorization; that is Verified Access.
Without an instance profile that allows SSM, the instance never shows up as a managed node.
